info.name: Clima Norm / Site Norm API — Full Collection
info.description:
Complete endpoint coverage for the wetland hydrology determination API (wetland-api backend). Built from a full source-code audit — every route file in src/modules/*/*.routes.js is represented here, nothing omitted.

SETUP:
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (see its description) to your running server, e.g. http://localhost:5000/api/v1 for local, or https://api.sitenorm.com/api/v1 for production.
2. Run Auth > Signup, then Auth > Verify OTP (after signup) with the real code emailed to you, OR just run Auth > Signin if you already have a verified account. Either one automatically saves the JWT into the `token` variable via a test script — every other request already uses {{token}} automatically, no manual copy-pasting required.
3. Requests marked [Admin] require the logged-in user to have role:admin in the database — a normal signup will NOT have this. You'll need to manually flip a test user's role to 'admin' directly in MongoDB to test those.
4. Public endpoints (marked noauth) work with no token at all — useful for confirming the server is reachable before debugging auth.

Re-sends a fresh signup-verification OTP to an unverified account.

Returns a JWT for a verified account. If the account isn't verified yet, this returns 403 and auto-sends a fresh OTP instead of a token.

The test script below auto-saves the token into {{token}} so every other request in this collection picks it up automatically.
Emails a password-reset OTP (separate from the signup OTP).

Confirms the reset code is valid. Note: reset-password re-validates email+otp itself and does not actually require the resetToken this returns — you can go straight to Reset Password with the same otp.
Sets a new password using the still-valid reset OTP (10 minute expiry from when Forgot Password was called).

item.name: Evaluations

request.description: PRIMARY endpoint. Runs the full NRCS Procedure 2 determination from GPS coordinates: reverse-geocodes county, finds nearest AgACIS station(s) with valid WETS data (falls back to triangulating 3 nearest stations if the closest lacks data), pulls rainfall + soil map unit + growing season, and returns the full determination. This is what Quick Search calls directly.
Same result shape as /calculate, but resolves stations by state+county name (or 5-digit FIPS) instead of GPS. Uses the county centroid for soil lookup if no station has data directly in the county.

Saves a previously-calculated evaluation result against the logged-in user's account.

IMPORTANT — how to build the body: in the /calculate response, the top level is `{ "success": true, "data": { ... } }`. Copy ONLY what's INSIDE that `data` key — i.e. start from `simpleLabel` and end at its matching closing brace — and paste THAT as the entire body here. Do NOT keep a `data` wrapper around it; `simpleLabel`, `location`, `observationDate`, etc. must be top-level keys of this request body, not nested one level down. A body shaped like `{ "data": { ... } }` will fail with 'Path `location.lon` is required' even though location is right there — the server is looking for it at the top level.
Flat list of the logged-in user's saved evaluations, most recent first.
Full detail for one saved evaluation — same response shape as /calculate. Auto-fails with 404 if the evaluation belongs to a different user.
Deletes one saved evaluation. Scoped to the logged-in user — cannot delete another user's evaluation.
Admin-only. Every user's evaluations, paginated, with optional ?status= (matches simpleLabel, e.g. 'Normal') and ?state= filters, plus aggregate stats. Requires a JWT for a user with role:admin.

item.description: The core feature: NRCS Procedure 2 wetland climatic determination. calculate and calculate-by-location are the two ways to run a determination; save/saved/:id/delete manage a user's history.

item.name: Subscription

request.description:
Simulates a RevenueCat webhook delivery. In production this is called by RevenueCat's servers, authenticated via an 'Authorization' header matching REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET (add that header manually here if the env var is set). app_user_id must be a real User _id from your database for the status update to actually apply to a user — otherwise the event is still recorded but no user is updated.

Try other event types by changing `type` to: RENEWAL, CANCELLATION, EXPIRATION, BILLING_ISSUE, REFUND, REFUND_REVERSED, TEST. For TRANSFER, use the separate example below — it has a different payload shape (no app_user_id at all).

TRANSFER events use a different field shape than every other RevenueCat event — no app_user_id, only transferred_from/transferred_to arrays (per RevenueCat's official docs). The old owner's status is set to expired, the new owner's to active. Both IDs must be real User _ids to see the effect.

Admin-only. Current subscription status per user. ?status= filters to one status (active/cancelled/expired/billing_issue/refunded/none); omit it to see everyone with any subscription history. Response includes aggregate `stats` counts by status.

Admin-only. Full transaction/event history (what the admin dashboard's 'transaction history list' is built from). Optional ?userId= to scope to one user, ?eventType= to filter by RevenueCat event type.

item.description: RevenueCat webhook (records purchase/cancellation/refund/transfer events and updates user status) + admin visibility into subscribers and transaction history.
